name: Copenhagen City Hall
description: The red-brick city hall and the big square in front, next to Tivoli. Inside is an astronomical clock, and the tower can be climbed.

name: Højbro Plads
description: An old-town square with a statue of Bishop Absalon on horseback, facing across the canal to Christiansborg Palace.

name: Kongens Nytorv
description: Copenhagen’s largest square, at the head of Nyhavn, with an equestrian statue of King Christian V in the middle.

name: Royal Danish Theatre
places: Royal Danish Theatre (Old Stage), Kongens Nytorv
description: The national theatre’s 1874 building on Kongens Nytorv, the home stage of the Royal Danish Ballet.

name: Little Mermaid
description: A small bronze statue of the fairy-tale mermaid, sitting on a rock by the harbour at Langelinie since 1913.

name: Radisson Collection Royal Hotel
description: A 1960 modernist hotel tower opposite Tivoli, with furniture and fittings designed by the same architect as the building.

name: Assistens Cemetery
description: A leafy cemetery in Nørrebro that locals use as a park, and the resting place of many well-known Danes, Kierkegaard among them.

name: Danish Jewish Museum
description: A museum of Danish Jewish history, including the 1943 rescue to Sweden, with an angular interior built inside an old royal boathouse.

name: Nyhavn
description: A 17th-century canal lined with colourful old townhouses, wooden ships and outdoor cafés, running from Kongens Nytorv to the harbour.

name: CopenHill
description: A waste-to-energy power plant with an artificial ski slope, a hiking trail and a climbing wall on its roof and walls.
